title: Level 1: Observability Signal Lanes
subtitle: How metrics, logs, traces, events, and operations workflows connect

nodes.label: Observability Signals
nodes.definition: A connected model for reading system behavior through multiple signal lanes.
nodes.whyItMatters: No single signal is enough for reliable operations decisions.
nodes.safeSentence: I explain observability as combining metrics, logs, traces, and events with response workflows.
nodes.commonTrap: Treating one dashboard or one metric as full truth.

note.summary: Hub node for Level 1 signal-lane thinking.

nodes.label: Metrics
nodes.definition: Numeric time-series data about utilization, performance, and error patterns.
nodes.whyItMatters: Metrics reveal trend and threshold changes quickly.
nodes.safeSentence: Metrics tell me what is changing over time and where risk may be rising.
nodes.commonTrap: Reading averages alone without percentiles or context.

note.summary: Fast health and capacity trend signal.

nodes.label: Logs
nodes.definition: Event records that describe what happened in systems and applications.
nodes.whyItMatters: Logs add incident context and evidence for troubleshooting.
nodes.safeSentence: Logs tell me what happened before, during, and after an issue.
nodes.commonTrap: Collecting logs without structure, retention plan, or correlation.

nodes.label: Traces
nodes.definition: Request-flow visibility across services showing latency and failure points.
nodes.whyItMatters: Traces isolate bottlenecks in distributed paths.
nodes.safeSentence: Traces show where a request traveled and where time or failure occurred.
nodes.commonTrap: Claiming deep tracing ownership before hands-on evidence.

nodes.label: Events
nodes.definition: Important change markers such as deploys, scaling actions, or incidents.
nodes.whyItMatters: Events explain why telemetry shifts at specific times.
nodes.safeSentence: Events mark important changes that explain signal movement.
nodes.commonTrap: Ignoring change events when analyzing metric spikes.

nodes.label: APM
nodes.definition: Application performance monitoring that ties transactions to user and service impact.
nodes.whyItMatters: APM connects symptom data to application behavior.
nodes.safeSentence: My enterprise APM background helps me interpret service behavior and impact.
nodes.commonTrap: Calling APM and observability identical concepts.

nodes.label: Infrastructure Monitoring
nodes.definition: Monitoring hosts, containers, CPU, memory, disk, and network behavior.
nodes.whyItMatters: Infrastructure health sets the baseline for service reliability.
nodes.safeSentence: Infrastructure monitoring watches host and container resource behavior.
nodes.commonTrap: Focusing only on CPU while ignoring memory, disk, or network pressure.

nodes.label: Cloud Monitoring
nodes.definition: Monitoring managed cloud services and cloud-native dependencies.
nodes.whyItMatters: Cloud services introduce platform-specific performance and reliability signals.
nodes.safeSentence: Cloud monitoring tracks managed service behavior and platform-level risks.

nodes.label: OpenTelemetry
nodes.definition: Vendor-neutral pattern for collecting and routing telemetry signals.
nodes.whyItMatters: It standardizes telemetry collection across tools and environments.
nodes.safeSentence: I use OpenTelemetry as the modern collection pattern and I am building practical depth.

nodes.label: Dashboards + Alerts + Runbooks
nodes.definition: Visibility, notification, and response guidance working together.
nodes.whyItMatters: Signals must lead to clear human action.
nodes.safeSentence: Dashboards make signals visible, alerts decide attention, and runbooks guide action.

nodes.label: Capacity Headroom
nodes.definition: Remaining resource margin used for planning and risk prevention.
nodes.whyItMatters: Headroom turns monitoring from reactive to proactive.
nodes.safeSentence: Capacity headroom helps translate telemetry into planning decisions.
nodes.commonTrap: Discussing capacity without demand trend and risk bands.

nodes.label: RCA / Troubleshooting
nodes.definition: Systematic process to connect symptoms to likely causes and recovery actions.
nodes.whyItMatters: Structured RCA improves reliability learning and repeatability.
nodes.safeSentence: RCA connects symptoms to likely causes using multiple signals.
nodes.commonTrap: Jumping to root-cause conclusions from one data source.

nodes.label: Safe Career Positioning
nodes.definition: Accurate interview positioning that separates proven strengths from active learning areas.
nodes.whyItMatters: Honest positioning builds trust and avoids overclaim risk.
nodes.safeSentence: My strong base is enterprise telemetry/APM/capacity, and I am actively building modern cloud-observability depth.
nodes.commonTrap: Claiming production ownership of OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana, Kubernetes, GPU monitoring, Terraform, CloudFormation, or cloud-native SRE before evidence.

nodes.label: Prometheus / Grafana / CloudWatch / Splunk / Dynatrace
nodes.definition: Common platform families for metrics, visualization, cloud monitoring, and observability workflows.
nodes.whyItMatters: Knowing tool-fit helps select the right workflow for each context.
nodes.safeSentence: I can explain where these tools fit while building practical ownership step by step.
nodes.commonTrap: Confusing conceptual familiarity with production platform ownership.

paths.label: Level 1 Signal Lanes Walk
paths.description: A practical orientation path through the major observability signal lanes and safe positioning.
